transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell indicates a serious fault that could lead to a fire. You must switch the appliance off and unplug it immediately; do not attempt to use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. While I can explain that this is often caused by lint buildup on the heater or a mechanical issue, these require professional dismantling and repair to fix safely.

plan: They asked: "is it safe to keep using it" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "giving off a burning smell". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
